And it’s not just her, it’s happening with everyone. I start a sentence with a clear destination in mind, and by the time I open my mouth, I’m taking detours through five different topics that have absolutely nothing to do with each other. Well, that’s the thing, doctor, it’s… it’s like I’m standing in a room with a hundred different televisions on at the exact same time, all tuned to different channels, and the volume is just blasting on every single one of them. In the exact second it happens, it makes perfect, absolute sense to me. The connections are so bright and loud in my head. 

But then I look at the other person, like my supervisor, and I see her face just completely blank, or confused, or annoyed, and I realize... I realize I lost her. I realize that the bridge I walked across in my mind is completely invisible to everyone else. And it’s terrifying, honestly, because I know I’m talking, I know the words are coming out of my mouth, but it’s like I’m a passenger in my own head. I just watch myself jump from the shift, to the soccer game, to the paint, to the charts, and I can't hit the brakes. I can't stop the train. Well, as for seeing things that aren't there, no, it's not like that. My eyes work perfectly fine. But... as for believing things that other people say aren't real? Yeah. Yes, actually. Because I notice things that everyone else just completely ignores or brushes off.

They’re watching to see if I’m unsafe.

They just don't see the reality of it. They completely buy the cover story. But I know it's happening. I know they're watching my every single move.

Putting thoughts in my head? No, no, I told you, my thoughts are my own. Nobody is beaming things into my brain or pulling them out. But anyway, I was trying to tell my supervisor about this incident during my overnight shift, and before I knew it, I was talking about the soccer game I watched last weekend, and then somehow that turned into me talking about the exact shade of blue they painted the walls in the break room, which is this weird, depressing grayish-blue, and then I was suddenly talking about patient charts and how the filing system is completely backwards. And I could just see it in her face, my supervisor’s face—she was completely lost. Her eyes just kind of glazed over, and she was looking at me like I was speaking a different language. And it’s not just her, it’s happening with everyone. I start a sentence with a clear destination in mind, and by the time I open my mouth, I’m taking detours through five different topics that have absolutely nothing to do with each other. It’s exhausting, honestly, and it’s making it impossible to just have a normal conversation or do my job without feeling like my brain is constantly misfiring.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe what it feels like inside your mind when your thoughts start to jump from one topic to another like that? Do you feel like you can’t control the shifts, or do they make sense to you at the time even if others don’t follow?\n\nPatient: Well, that’s the thing, doctor, it’s… it’s like I’m standing in a room with a hundred different televisions on at the exact same time, all tuned to different channels, and the volume is just blasting on every single one of them. And I’m trying to watch one show, right? Like, I’m trying to focus on telling you about how I can't keep my words straight, how I start talking about my overnight shift and then suddenly I'm talking about soccer, and then the depressing blue paint in the break room, and then the patient charts... but while I'm trying to say that, my brain is just flipping the channels on its own. \n\nIt feels completely out of my control. It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking, \"Oh, let me change the subject to the color of the wall now.\" It’s more like the wall color is suddenly the most important, urgent thing in the world, and it connects perfectly to the soccer game in my head because, I don't know, maybe the goalie's jersey was blue, and then the jersey reminds me of the scrubs we wear, which reminds me of the charts. In the exact second it happens, it makes perfect, absolute sense to me. The connections are so bright and loud in my head. \n\nBut then I look at the other person, like my supervisor, and I see her face just completely blank, or confused, or annoyed, and I realize... I realize I lost her. I realize that the bridge I walked across in my mind is completely invisible to everyone else. And it’s terrifying, honestly, because I know I’m talking, I know the words are coming out of my mouth, but it’s like I’m a passenger in my own head. I just watch myself jump from the shift, to the soccer game, to the paint, to the charts, and I can't hit the brakes. I can't stop the train. I just have to watch everyone get lost while I keep talking.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced things that others around you don't seem to notice—like hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or believing something is happening that others say isn't real?\n\nPatient: Well, as for seeing things that aren't there, no, it's not like that. My eyes work perfectly fine. But... as for believing things that other people say aren't real? Yeah. Yes, actually. Because I notice things that everyone else just completely ignores or brushes off. \n\nLike... okay, take my schedule at the hospital, for instance. I mentioned I work the overnight shifts, but lately, they just keep moving my hours around. They are constantly changing my shifts, pulling me from one ward to another. And if you ask anyone else, if you ask the other aides or the charge nurse, they all give me the exact same rehearsed line. They say, \"Oh, it's just staffing shortages, you know how it is, turnover is so high, nobody wants to work the night shift.\" And sure, people quit all the time, the job is an absolute meat grinder, but... that’s not why they’re changing my schedule. I know that’s not why. \n\nI am absolutely sure the supervisors are doing it on purpose. They changed my shifts so they can isolate me and watch me. We have these security cameras all over the unit—these little black dome ones mounted on the ceiling, right? There's one by the med room, one pointing down the East hall where the high-acuity patients are, and one right over the main nurses' station. And I know for a fact they sit in their office, the one behind the locked double doors with the frosted glass, just staring at the monitors, watching me through those unit cameras. They’re watching to see if I’m unsafe. \n\nI can literally feel them doing it. When I’m walking down the hall doing my 15-minute bed checks, I can feel the lens zooming in on the back of my neck. They're just waiting for me to make a mistake, waiting for me to do something dangerous or unsafe so they can catch me on tape. And I try to explain this to the other guys on my shift! I tell my coworker, I say, \"Look at the angle of the camera over the charting desk, look how it’s pointed exactly at my chair and nowhere else,\" but they just sigh and tell me I need to get more sleep, and then they go right back to complaining about the staffing shortages. They just don't see the reality of it. They completely buy the cover story. But I know it's happening. I know they're watching my every single move.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by an outside force, or that events or actions around you are specifically directed at you, even if others don’t see it that way?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, that’s… that’s exactly what I was just trying to explain to you about the schedule and the cameras! Like, I don't know about thoughts being put into my head by an outside force, my thoughts are my own, even if they're a mess right now. But events being directed specifically at me? Yes. Absolutely yes. That is exactly what is happening with my supervisors. \n\nLike I just said, they are moving my shifts around, and it is completely, one hundred percent directed at me. It’s not random. It’s not... it's not what everyone else keeps telling me it is. My coworkers, the other aides, they all just parrot the exact same excuse: 'Oh, it's the staffing shortages, you know hospitals are understaffed right now, they just need a warm body on the floor.' But they aren't the ones living it! They aren't the ones being specifically targeted by the administration. \n\nI know for an absolute fact that the supervisors changed my shifts specifically so they can isolate me and watch me through those unit cameras. It’s like the whole hospital schedule revolves around keeping tabs on me. Because, think about it... if they put me on the overnight shift, down on the East hall, there's way less foot traffic, right? Fewer doctors rounding, no family members visiting. It's just me, the patients sleeping, and the cameras. And they sit up there behind those frosted glass doors in the main office, watching the security monitors, just waiting to see if I'm unsafe. \n\nThey are literally orchestrating the whole hospital roster just to test me, to see if I'll make a mistake or do something dangerous. Every single time the new schedule gets posted on the corkboard by the breakroom time clock, I can see the pattern. The way my name gets crossed out and moved from a Tuesday day shift to a Thursday night shift... it's not a coincidence. It's an action directed right at me. It's them saying, 'We are watching you.' And it doesn't matter how many times people tell me it's just a staffing shortage, I know the truth. I know they are doing it to me on purpose.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like someone is putting thoughts into your mind or taking thoughts out of it, or do you believe things that other people would say are completely untrue, outside of what you've already described about your supervisors and the cameras?\n\nPatient: Putting thoughts in my head? No, no, I told you, my thoughts are my own. Nobody is beaming things into my brain or pulling them out. But... when you ask about believing things other people say are untrue, and you say \"outside of the supervisors\"... Doctor, you have to understand, I can't just move past the supervisors and the cameras. I can't just drop it because it's... it's everything. It dictates my entire life right now. You ask if there's something else, but why would there need to be something else when this massive thing is happening to me every single night? \n\nPeople keep telling me I'm wrong. My mom, the other aides, the charge nurses... they all give me the exact same line. \"Oh, it's just the staffing shortages, everyone is working weird hours, we're down three guys this month.\" But they aren't looking at the facts. They aren't looking at the actual schedule printed on that cheap glossy paper pinned up in the breakroom. I am absolutely sure they changed my shifts—specifically mine, isolating my name on that sheet—just to watch me. \n\nThey deliberately put me on these dead hours, like 11 PM to 7 AM, on the quietest wards, and I know they are staring through those unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. Like, if I hesitate for even a second while checking a patient's door, or if I take too long in the supply closet grabbing fresh linens... I know they're watching the monitors behind those frosted glass doors. They want to see if I'm a danger, if I'm somehow unsafe to be around the patients. And everyone else just shrugs it off! They just completely brush it off as administrative turnover or whatever corporate buzzword the hospital is using this week. But I know it. I know it in my bones. They are watching me to see if I'm unsafe, and I can't just talk about something else or answer another question when I know that camera lens is literally pointed at my back for eight hours straight.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that your actions are being controlled by someone or something outside of yourself, like you're a puppet or being manipulated?\n\nPatient: Like a puppet? No... no, nobody is pulling strings attached to my arms or legs. I walk where I want to walk, I move my own body. But... manipulated? Yes. Absolutely yes. I am being manipulated, but not... not in the weird sci-fi way you're making it sound. \n\nDoctor, it’s what I keep trying to tell you! I feel like we're just going in circles here because you keep asking me all these bizarre questions about mind control and puppets and outside forces, and I keep trying to get you to understand what is actually, literally happening to me right now. You're trying to move on to something else, but I can't move on. The manipulation is the schedule. It’s the supervisors. \n\nI know I keep bringing it up, but how can I not? They are manipulating my entire life by orchestrating where I am and when. They changed my shifts—specifically mine, pulling me off days and shoving me onto the graveyard rotation—to trap me on the floor at 3 AM. And my coworkers, they just... they give me that exact same tired excuse every single time I try to show them the pattern. They say, \"Oh man, it's just the staffing shortages, you know how high the turnover is, management is just scrambling.\" It makes me want to scream because they are so blind to it! \n\nI am completely, one hundred percent sure the supervisors are doing this on purpose. They manipulate the roster so they can isolate me and watch me through the unit cameras. They aren't controlling my hands, but they are controlling my environment. They set up this whole elaborate trap, sticking me in the quietest part of the hospital, just so they can sit up there behind those frosted glass doors and stare at the security monitors. They are watching to see if I'm unsafe. They're waiting for me to crack, waiting for me to do something dangerous around the patients so they have it on tape. So no, I'm not a puppet, but they are absolutely manipulating my life to watch me, and I just don't understand why nobody else can see it when it's right in front of their faces.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being broadcasted for others to hear?\n\nPatient: I feel like a broken record here, man. No. No one is inserting thoughts into my brain, and no, my thoughts aren't on some loudspeaker or being broadcasted on the radio for people to hear. I literally just told you my thoughts are my own. You keep asking me about mind reading and all this crazy sci-fi stuff, but you are completely ignoring the actual, real-life thing that is destroying my life right now! \n\nWhy do you keep asking about what's inside my head when I am telling you about what is happening out there on the floor? I don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you. I am absolutely, one hundred percent sure the supervisors changed my shifts specifically to watch me through those unit cameras. You keep trying to make it about my brain, but it's about the cameras! They sit in that main office, behind the frosted glass, and they watch the security feeds for hours just to see if I'm unsafe. That's what's happening. \n\nAnd everyone, literally everyone—my mom, the charge nurses, the other aides—they just keep feeding me the exact same garbage line. \"Oh, it's just staffing shortages, we're down a few guys this week, management is just filling holes.\" It is not normal! It is not a staffing shortage! They isolated me on the night shift on purpose so they can watch me to see if I'm going to do something dangerous around the patients. You keep asking me if my thoughts are being broadcasted, but they don't need to hear my thoughts, Doctor, because they are watching my every single physical move on those monitors! Why won't you just listen to what I'm actually saying about the schedule?\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else or that your thoughts are being broadcasted so that others can hear them?\n\nPatient: Are you... did you just read the wrong question off your clipboard or something? You literally just asked me that! Like, two seconds ago! I just told you, no! No one is putting thoughts in my head, and no one is broadcasting them so people can hear them.
